definition_zh: 昆虫学家；研究昆虫的专家
definition_en: a scientist who studies insects
core_image: 一个人蹲在草丛边，手里拿着小瓶与镊子，眼睛贴着一片叶子背面看不动的小点
scene: 天还没亮，研究者已经蹲在湿地边，把夜里落进诱捕瓶的虫子一只只分装。 The entomologist sorted the catch by family before the heat made the specimens brittle.
sceneCN: 这里 entomologist 指「昆虫学家」（第 1 个义项：以科学研究方式研究昆虫的人）；句意为昆虫学家趁高温使标本变脆之前，把捕获物按科分拣。

pos.zh: 昆虫学家；（某一类群的）昆虫研究专家

senses.title: A scientist who studies insects
senses.titleCN: 以科学方式研究昆虫的人
senses.definition: a person trained to study the biology, classification and ecology of insects
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、研究昆虫生物学、分类与生态的人
senses.example: The entomologist sorted the catch by family.
senses.exampleCN: 昆虫学家把捕获物按科分拣。
senses.why: entomology plus -ist marks the practitioner, so the word names a person by the discipline practised.
senses.whyCN: entomology 加 -ist 标记从事者，因此这个词以所从事的学科来命名一个人。

senses.title: A specialist in one insect group
senses.definition: a researcher who works on a single order, family or genus rather than on insects generally
senses.definitionCN: 只研究某一个目、科或属、而非泛研究昆虫的研究者
senses.example: She is the entomologist for the beetle collection.
senses.exampleCN: 她是甲虫收藏方面的昆虫学家。
senses.why: specialisation is expressed by the object added, while the title itself stays general.
senses.whyCN: 专化由所加的对象表达，而头衔本身保持通用。

senses.title: A field surveyor of insect populations
senses.titleCN: 野外昆虫种群的调查者
senses.definition: a person who counts and samples insects in the field for monitoring or conservation
senses.definitionCN: 为监测或保育而在野外计数与取样昆虫的人
senses.example: The entomologist walked the same transect every week for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这位昆虫学家一年里每周走同一条样带。
senses.why: the discipline's main evidence comes from field samples, so the practitioner is often met as a surveyor.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科的主要证据来自野外取样，因此实践者常以调查者形象出现。

senses.title: A forensic expert reading insect evidence
senses.titleCN: 解读昆虫证据的法医专家
senses.definition: a specialist who uses insects on a body or at a scene to estimate time and circumstances
senses.definitionCN: 利用尸体或现场上的昆虫推断时间与情形的专家
senses.example: The entomologist was called before the body was moved.
senses.exampleCN: 尸体被移动之前，昆虫学家就被叫到了现场。
senses.why: the same training is applied to legal questions, and the title follows the person rather than the setting.
senses.whyCN: 同样的训练被用于法律问题，头衔随人走而不随场合变。

senses.title: A museum curator of insect collections
senses.definition: a person responsible for naming, preserving and organising a reference collection
senses.definitionCN: 负责命名、保存与整理参考收藏的人
senses.example: The entomologist found the type specimen mislabelled.
senses.exampleCN: 这位昆虫学家发现模式标本标签贴错了。
senses.why: collections are the discipline's archive, so curation is part of the professional role.
senses.whyCN: 收藏是该学科的档案，因此管理收藏是职业角色的一部分。

senses.title: A medical or veterinary specialist
senses.titleCN: 医学或兽医方向的专家
senses.definition: a specialist in insects that bite, parasitise or transmit disease
senses.definitionCN: 研究叮咬、寄生或传播疾病的昆虫的专家
senses.example: A medical entomologist traced the outbreak to standing water.
senses.exampleCN: 一位医学昆虫学家把疫情追溯到积水。
senses.why: public health employs the same title with a qualifier, because the object of study is still insects.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生以限定语使用同一头衔，因为研究对象仍是昆虫。

senses.title: A knowledgeable amateur
senses.definition: a non-professional who has acquired reliable expert knowledge of a local insect fauna
senses.definitionCN: 在本地昆虫区系上获得可靠专门知识的非职业者
senses.example: The county's best entomologist is a retired postal clerk.
senses.exampleCN: 这个郡最好的昆虫学家是一位退休邮局职员。
senses.why: the title tracks knowledge rather than employment, so long observation can earn it.
senses.whyCN: 这个头衔跟知识走而不跟职位走，因此长期观察也能赢来。

senses.title: Informal: the person who knows the bugs
senses.definition: loosely, anyone consulted about an insect problem, such as a pest-control specialist
senses.definitionCN: 泛指任何就昆虫问题被咨询的人，如害虫防治专家
senses.example: They called the entomologist before spraying the warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在给仓库喷药之前先叫来了昆虫专家。
senses.why: in everyday use the word marks expertise about insects rather than a research career.
senses.whyCN: 在日常用法里，这个词标记的是关于昆虫的专长，而非研究生涯。

intro.en: Entomologist is entomology plus the agent suffix -ist, so it simply means the person who practises the study of insects.
intro.cn: entomologist 是 entomology 加施事后缀 -ist，意思就是从事昆虫研究的人。

items.en: Entomon 'insect' comes from en- 'in' plus temnein 'to cut', naming a body divided into sections.
items.cn: entomon「昆虫」由 en-「在内」加 temnein「切」构成，命名身体分成段落的生物。

items.en: Greek -logia passed into English as -logy, and from the seventeenth century it named learned fields of study.
items.cn: 希腊 -logia 进入英语作 -logy，自 17 世纪起用于命名各门学术领域。

items.en: The suffix -ist, from Greek -istes, marks a person engaged in an activity, as in botanist and geologist.
items.cn: 后缀 -ist 出自希腊 -istes，标记从事某种活动的人，如 botanist、geologist。

items.en: Entomologist became a recognised occupational title in the nineteenth century as museums and universities hired specialists.
items.cn: 19 世纪博物馆与大学开始聘用专家，entomologist 成为被承认的职业头衔。

items.en: Forensic, medical and consulting qualifiers appeared as the expertise was applied outside academia.
items.cn: 随着这一专长在学术界之外应用，forensic、medical、consulting 等限定语出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English record of entomologist is not firmly dated, and Greek temnein lacks a fully settled Indo-European root.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：entomologist 最早英语书证年代不确定，希腊 temnein 的印欧词根亦无完全定论。

note.en: Group one separates the entomologist from the other words of the same family; group two separates the specialist from neighbouring experts.
note.cn: 第一组区分 entomologist 与同族其它词；第二组区分这位专家与邻近领域的专家。

entries.definition: The field itself; the -ist person practices it, so the two cannot replace each other in a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 学科本身；-ist 者从事它，二者在句中不能互换。

entries.definition: Describes what relates to the field, as in entomological survey; it never names a person.
entries.definitionCN: 描述与该领域相关的事物，如昆虫学调查；它从不命名人。

entries.definition: An etymologist studies word origins; the similarity to entomologist is a classic source of confusion.
entries.definitionCN: etymologist 研究词源；与 entomologist 的相似是经典的混淆来源。

entries.definition: The animal, from the Latin calque; the person who studies it carries the Greek-based title.
entries.definitionCN: 动物本身，出自拉丁仿译；研究它的人则用希腊式头衔。

entries.definition: A zoologist studies animals in general; an entomologist is a zoologist specialised in one class.
entries.definitionCN: zoologist 研究整个动物界；entomologist 是专攻一个纲的动物学家。

entries.definition: Studies spiders and their relatives, which are not insects; the title is a separate specialism.
entries.definitionCN: 研究蜘蛛及其近亲，它们不是昆虫；这是另一个专门领域。

entries.definition: An ecologist studies relations between organisms and habitat, and may work with insects without being an entomologist.
entries.definitionCN: 生态学家研究生物与生境的关系，可能研究昆虫但不是昆虫学家。

entries.definition: A pest-control worker removes infestations; the title marks a service trade, not a research qualification.
entries.definitionCN: 害虫防治人员清除虫害；这个头衔标记服务行业，而非研究资历。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real agent suffix, real professional titles and a real confusable pair.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实施事后缀、真实职业头衔与一对真实易混词。

normal.en: entomology + -ist: the person who does the study.
normal.cn: entomology + -ist：从事这门研究的人。

normal.en: The family runs entomology, entomologist, entomological, entomofauna.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 entomology、entomologist、entomological、entomofauna。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: field entomologist, forensic entomologist, medical entomologist.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：野外昆虫学家、法医昆虫学家、医学昆虫学家。

normal.en: The -ist suffix also builds botanist, zoologist and geologist.
normal.cn: -ist 后缀还构成 botanist、zoologist、geologist。

normal.en: Entomologist and etymologist differ by one letter and by an entire field.
normal.cn: entomologist 与 etymologist 差一个字母，也差一整门学科。

abstract.en: Picture a person who can name every small thing in a meadow.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人能叫出草地上每一样小东西的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a notebook filled with dates and weather, one line per sighting.
abstract.cn: 想象一本记满日期与天气的本子，每次目击一行。

abstract.en: Picture a courtroom where the expert evidence is a fly on a leaf.
abstract.cn: 想象一个法庭，专家证据是叶上的一只蝇。

examples.en: An entomologist can identify the species from a single wing.
examples.cn: 昆虫学家能凭一片翅识别物种。

examples.en: The park employs an entomologist to monitor pollinators.
examples.cn: 公园聘用一位昆虫学家监测传粉者。

examples.en: He became an entomologist after raising moths as a boy.
examples.cn: 他小时候养蛾，后来成了昆虫学家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「entomo（昆虫）+ logist（研究者）」——研究虫子的人 → 昆虫学家

root: entomology（希腊 entomon「昆虫」+ -logia「学问」）+ -ist（从事者）；entomon = en-（在内）+ temnein（切）。首见年代与 temnein 词根存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one expert: a person studies insects as a science, then narrows to a group, walks a field transect, reads evidence for a court, curates a collection, serves public health, earns the title as an amateur, and finally is anyone consulted about a bug.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一位专家展开：此人以科学方式研究昆虫，随后收窄到某一类群、走野外样带、为法庭解读证据、管理收藏、服务公共卫生、以业余身份赢得头衔，最后成为任何被问及虫子的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person crouched by a leaf, naming a speck nobody else can see.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人蹲在叶旁，叫出别人看不见的那一粒小点的名字。

branches.en: TRAINED EYE: general science first, then a narrow specialism.
branches.cn: 受训的眼：先是通用科学，再是狭窄专攻。

branches.en: FIELD PRESENCE: the same eye counting along a transect.
branches.cn: 野外在场：同一双眼沿样带计数。

branches.en: SERVICE ROLES: court and clinic borrow the expertise.
branches.cn: 服务角色：法庭与诊所借用这份专长。

branches.en: ARCHIVE KEEPER: collections are the discipline's memory.
branches.cn: 档案守护：收藏是学科的记性。

branches.en: TITLE BY KNOWLEDGE: a patient observer or a consulted trader may carry the name.
branches.cn: 凭知识得名：耐心的观察者或被咨询的从业者也可带此名。

intro.en: Entomologist is a Greek-derived compound plus a Greek agent suffix, so each element marks either the object or the person.
intro.cn: entomologist 是希腊来源的复合词加希腊施事后缀，每一成分标记对象或人。

latinIntro.en: The word is Greek throughout; Latin insectum is the calque of entomon and appears in the parallel English word insect.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词全程为希腊语；拉丁 insectum 是 entomon 的仿译，见于平行的英语词 insect。

items.example: The prefix marks a body cut inward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记向内切开的身体。

items.example: The root supplies the image of segmentation.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供分节的意象。

items.example: Entomon is the object of the study.

items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名这门领域。
昆虫学家把模式标本插针固定。

items.example: The entomofauna of the delta was surveyed twice.
items.exampleCN: 三角洲的昆虫区系被调查过两次。

items.example: Entomophilous flowers usually have colour and scent.

definition_zh: 入口；门口；进入；入场；使入迷；使出神
definition_en: a door or gate that you go through to enter a place; the act of entering; to fill someone with wonder so that they cannot think of anything else
core_image: 一扇敞开的门：人穿过它走进去，或被门里的景象牢牢吸住
scene: 暴雨中她终于找到博物馆侧面的那扇小门。She stood at the entrance of the museum, shaking the rain off her umbrella.
sceneCN: 这里 entrance 是「入口、门口」（第 1 个义项：进入一个地方的门或通道）；句意是她站在博物馆入口处抖落伞上的雨水。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「令人着迷的」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「入迷；出神」
同源词形变化，义为「进入；条目」

senses.title: A door or gate by which you enter a place
senses.definition: a door, gate, or passage that you go through to get into a building or place
senses.definitionCN: 进入建筑物或场地时穿过的门、大门或通道
senses.example: We waited for her at the main entrance of the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站正门口等她。
senses.why: The word comes from enter plus the noun suffix -ance, so the core image is the point where entering physically happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 enter（进入）加名词后缀 -ance 构成，核心意象就是「进入」动作实际发生的那扇门。

senses.title: The act of entering a place
senses.definition: the act of going into a place, or the right to do so
senses.definitionCN: 走进某个地方的行为，或获准进入的权利
senses.example: Entrance to the exhibition is free on Mondays.
senses.exampleCN: 展览入场周一免费。
senses.why: Because the suffix -ance turns an action into a noun, the word also names the act of entering itself, not just the doorway.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ance 能把动作名词化，所以 entrance 也指「进入」这个行为本身，而不仅仅是门口。

senses.title: Admission to a school or organization
senses.definition: the right or permission to join a school, university, or organization
senses.definitionCN: 加入学校、大学或组织的权利或许可
senses.example: She passed the entrance exam and entered the university.
senses.exampleCN: 她通过入学考试，进入了那所大学。
senses.why: Entering an institution is entering a gate in a figurative sense, so the act of entering extends to admission.
senses.whyCN: 进入一所学校就像穿过一扇比喻的门，「进入」的动作自然延伸为「录取、准入」。

senses.title: A person's first appearance before an audience
senses.definition: the moment when an actor or performer comes onto a stage
senses.definitionCN: 演员或表演者登上舞台的时刻
senses.example: The actor missed his entrance cue in the second act.
senses.exampleCN: 演员在第二幕错过了登场提示。
senses.why: Stepping onto a stage is entering a space in front of an audience, so the act of entering narrows to a theatrical appearance.
senses.whyCN: 走上舞台就是当着观众「进入」一个空间，「进入」于是具体化为戏剧中的登场。

senses.title: To fill someone with great wonder
senses.definition: to fill someone with delight and wonder so that they forget everything else
senses.definitionCN: 使某人充满喜悦与惊奇，以至忘掉周围的一切
senses.example: The children were entranced by the magician's tricks.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们被魔术师的戏法迷住了。
senses.why: As a verb, entrance means to make someone enter a trance-like state of wonder, shifting from doors to a spellbound mind.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时，entrance 表示让人「进入」一种入迷出神的状态，语义从门转到了被迷住的心。

senses.title: To charm so deeply that one cannot look away
senses.definition: to charm or fascinate someone completely
senses.definitionCN: 彻底迷住或吸引住某人
senses.example: The audience sat entranced throughout the whole performance.
senses.exampleCN: 整场演出中观众都看得入了神。
senses.why: This grows out of the trance image: fascination is a trance that holds the eyes and mind at the doorway of attention.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项从「出神」意象生长出来：着迷就是一种把眼睛和心牢牢拴在注意力门口的入迷状态。

senses.title: A movement inward in dance or ritual
senses.definition: a formal movement of walking into a room or ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 走进房间或仪式现场的一种正式动作
senses.example: The bride made a slow entrance as the music began.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐响起，新娘缓缓入场。
senses.why: Ceremonies turn the simple act of entering into a performed movement, extending the stage sense to formal occasions.
senses.whyCN: 仪式把「进入」这个简单动作变成一场表演，登场义由此延伸到婚礼等正式场合。

senses.title: A way in as a point of access
senses.definition: a way or means of getting access to something such as a career or a topic
senses.definitionCN: 通往事业、话题等的途径或手段
senses.example: The internship gave her an entrance into journalism.
senses.exampleCN: 这段实习为她打开了进入新闻业的大门。
senses.why: A doorway can be metaphorical, so entrance names any path that lets someone get into a field or subject.
senses.whyCN: 门可以比喻化，entrance 于是也指任何让人得以进入某个领域或话题的途径。

intro.en: Entrance as a noun comes from the verb enter plus the French-style noun suffix -ance; the verb sense meaning to fascinate was formed later from the noun, suggesting a state one enters.
intro.cn: 名词 entrance 由动词 enter 加法语式名词后缀 -ance 构成；表「使入迷」的动词用法较晚由名词引申而来，意为让人进入一种出神状态。

items.en: Latin intrare meant to go in, formed from intro (inward) and related to intra (within), the root behind English enter.
items.cn: 拉丁语 intrare 意为「进入」，由 intro（向内）构成，与 intra（在内）同族，是英语 enter 的词根来源。

items.en: Old French entrer carried the same meaning of going in, and the suffix -ance formed action nouns from verbs.
items.cn: 古法语 entrer 保留「进入」之义，后缀 -ance 则从动词构成表动作的名词。

items.en: English enter was borrowed from Old French in the Middle English period, and entrance appeared in the sixteenth century as the noun of entering.
items.cn: 英语 enter 在中古英语时期借自古法语；名词 entrance 于十六世纪出现，表示「进入」。

items.en: By the late sixteenth century entrance meant both the doorway and the act of entering, including admission to institutions.
items.cn: 十六世纪末，entrance 同时指门口与进入行为，并延伸出「入学、准入」之义。

items.en: The verb entrance meaning to put into a trance arose in the seventeenth century, generally explained as entrance (the noun) used as a verb, blending with the word trance.
items.cn: 十七世纪出现动词 entrance「使入迷」，一般认为是名词转作动词使用，并与 trance（出神）一词互相影响而成。

items.en: Today the noun stress falls on the first syllable for the doorway sense, while the fascinating verb is stressed on the second, keeping the two uses distinct.
items.cn: 今天名词「门口」义重音在第一个音节，动词「使入迷」义重音在第二个音节，两种用法靠重音区分。

note.en: Entrance has a look-alike cousin and a family of near-meaning words about doors, admission, and fascination.
note.cn: entrance 有一个形近词，以及一组关于门、准入与着迷的近义词。

entries.definition: the act of entering, or an item written in a list or record
entries.definitionCN: 进入的行为，或记录、清单中的一条；与 entrance 同根，但更常指进入行为和条目

entries.definition: a passage or area leading to an entrance
entries.definitionCN: 通向入口的过道或区域；entrance 的复合扩展词

entries.definition: a half-awake state in which you are not aware of your surroundings
entries.definitionCN: 半睡半醒、浑然不觉周围的状态；动词 entrance 与其义相关，但拼写相近且词源交织，trance 本身另为一词

entries.definition: the area just inside a door of a building
entries.definitionCN: 进门后紧挨着门的区域；与入口义近，多用于美式英语

entries.definition: the space where a door opens into a room or building
entries.definitionCN: 门洞；门口，侧重门框形成的开口本身

entries.definition: to interest someone so much that they cannot look away
entries.definitionCN: 深深吸引；使着迷，与动词 entrance 的「使入迷」义相近但更常用

normalIntro.en: Five memory hooks built on the word family and real usage of entrance.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于词族与真实用法的记忆钩子。

normal.en: enter + -ance: the suffix turns the action of entering into the noun for the doorway itself.
normal.cn: enter + -ance：后缀把「进入」这个动作名词化，就成了「入口」这个词。

normal.en: entrance exam is the gate you must pass to enter a school.
normal.cn: entrance exam（入学考试）就是进入学校前必须穿过的那扇门。

normal.en: entrance fee: money paid at the door before you go in.
normal.cn: entrance fee（入场费）是进门之前在门口付的钱。

normal.en: make an entrance: actors enter the stage, so an entrance is also an appearance.
normal.cn: make an entrance：演员「进入」舞台，所以 entrance 也有「登场」之义。

normal.en: the verb entrance is enter + trance: it makes someone enter a trance of wonder.
normal.cn: 动词 entrance 可以拆成 enter + trance：让人「进入」一种着迷出神的状态。

abstract.en: Picture a glowing doorway that pulls people toward it like a magnet.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇发光的门，像磁铁一样把人往里吸——既是入口，也让人入迷。

abstract.en: Feel the moment you step through a gate: the boundary between outside and inside.
abstract.cn: 体会跨过大门那一刻：门就是外面与里面的分界线。

abstract.en: Imagine a viewer frozen at the theater door, unable to look away from the stage.
abstract.cn: 想象观众僵在剧场门口，眼睛再也离不开舞台——被「使入迷」的样子。

examples.en: The main entrance of the hotel faces the sea.
examples.cn: 酒店的正门面向大海。

examples.en: The audience was entranced by her violin solo.
examples.cn: 观众被她的小提琴独奏迷住了。

examples.en: His perfect score guaranteed his entrance to the top university.
examples.cn: 他的满分成绩确保了他进入那所顶尖大学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因缺死」——你因太想进去而「因缺死」在门口；进去了又被舞台迷得「因缺死」挪不开眼。谐音只是联想，与词源无关。

root: 源自拉丁语 intrare（进入），由 intro（向内）派生，与 intra（在内）同族；经古法语 entrer 进入英语，动词 enter + 名词后缀 -ance 构成 entrance；「使入迷」义一般认为由名词转类而来，并与 trance（出神）相互影响。

sensesIntro.en: From a physical doorway the word fans out to the act of entering, admission, stage appearance, and finally the verb sense of charming someone into a trance.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个具体的门出发，这个词扩展到进入行为、准入、舞台登场，最终落到动词义的「使人入迷出神」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doorway through which people or attention passes
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇门，人或注意力由此穿过

branches.en: The concrete door or gate of a building.
branches.cn: 建筑具体的门或大门。

branches.en: Entering widens into admission rights and entrance exams.
branches.cn: 进入行为扩展为准入权利与入学考试。

branches.en: Entering a stage becomes a performed appearance.
branches.cn: 进入舞台变成一场被观看的登场。

branches.en: The doorway turns metaphorical: a path into a career.
branches.cn: 门比喻化：成为进入某个行业的途径。

branches.en: Attention passes through the door of the mind into a trance.
branches.cn: 注意力穿过心灵之门，进入出神着迷的状态。

intro.en: Entrance is built from a French-learned verb plus a Latinate noun suffix, and its family shows how -ance names actions and states.
intro.cn: entrance 由一个借自古法语的动词加拉丁式名词后缀构成，其词族展示了 -ance 如何命名动作与状态。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root intr- means to go in, and it survives in a small family of English words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 intr- 意为「进入」，在英语中留下了一小族同源词。

items.meaningCN: 表动作、状态或性质的后缀
items.example: The entrance is on the left.

items.meaning: the act of entering or an item in a list
items.example: There is no entry in the log for today.
items.exampleCN: 日志里没有今天的记录。

items.meaning: money paid to go into a place
items.example: The entrance fee is ten yuan.

items.meaning: an exam for admission to a school
items.example: She is preparing for the entrance exam.
The patient received an intravenous drip.

items.meaning: a person whose attention turns inward
items.example: As an introvert, she recharges alone.
items.exampleCN: 作为内向者，她靠独处恢复精力。

items.meaning: to look inside one's own mind
items.example: He paused to introspect before answering.
items.exampleCN: 他停下来内省之后才回答。

items.meaning: to lead something in; to bring in for the first time
items.example: Let me introduce our new colleague.
items.exampleCN: 让我介绍一下我们的新同事。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「令人着迷的」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「入迷」
同根名词，义为「进入；条目」

definition_zh: （美式）主菜；（英式）开胃菜；进入的途径
definition_en: the main dish of a meal in American usage, or a way of being admitted to a group or activity
core_image: 菜单翻到中间那页，最贵的一盘被端上桌；另一层含义是有人替你把门推开
scene: 这家店的主菜选择很少，多数客人转而点面食。The entree list was short, so many guests chose pasta.
sceneCN: 这里 entree 是「主菜」（第 1 个义项：美式用法中的正餐主盘）；句意：主菜清单很短，许多客人选了面食。

pos.zh: 主菜；开胃菜；进入的途径

senses.title: The main dish of a meal
senses.definition: the principal dish served in the middle of a meal, listed on menus
senses.definitionCN: 正餐中段上桌的主盘，通常列在菜单上
senses.example: Pick an entree before the soup arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 在汤上桌前选好主菜。
senses.why: The French word meant an entering, and the dish that enters the table is the one served in the middle.
senses.whyCN: 法语原义为进入，而登上桌的那道菜就成了中段的主盘。

senses.title: A course served at the start of a meal
senses.definition: in British and formal use, the first small course after which the main dish follows
senses.definitionCN: 在英式与正式用法中指紧随其后的第一小盘
senses.example: The set menu begins with a cold entree.
senses.exampleCN: 套餐以一道冷头盘开场。
senses.why: Old French menus placed the entrée first, so the older English use kept the opening position.
senses.whyCN: 古法语菜单把 entrée 列在首位，因此较早的英语用法保留开席的位置。

senses.title: A way of being admitted to a group
senses.definition: something that gives a person access to a profession or social circle
senses.definitionCN: 使人得以进入某职业或社交圈的凭借
senses.example: A internship can be an entree into journalism.
senses.exampleCN: 实习可能成为进入新闻行业的门径。
senses.why: Transferred from the door of a dining room to the door of a career, the noun keeps the idea of being let in.
senses.whyCN: 从餐厅的门转移到职业的门，这个名词保留了被放入的概念。

intro.en: Entree is the French entrée, a noun of entering from entrer, which continues Latin intrare.
intro.cn: entree 即法语 entrée，表进入的名词，出自 entrer，承自拉丁语 intrare。

items.en: Intrare means to go into.
items.cn: intrare 意为进入。

items.en: Entrer and its noun entry carry the sense inward.
items.cn: entrer 及名词 entry 把词义带入法语。

items.en: French dining menus use entrée for the opening dish.
items.cn: 十七世纪法式菜单以 entrée 称首盘。

items.en: English cookery books borrow the word with the menu.
items.cn: 十八世纪英语食谱连同菜单借入该词。

items.en: American restaurants shift the term to the main plate.
items.cn: 十九世纪美国餐馆把该词转指主盘。

items.en: Figurative use names any door into a profession.
items.cn: 现代英语中以比喻指进入某行业的门径。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same entering stem; group two holds other course and access words.
note.cn: 第一组是同一进入词干的词；第二组是其他表示菜品或门路的词。

entries.definition: The written French form, still seen on menus that keep the accent.
entries.definitionCN: 保留重音符号的法语写法，菜单上仍可见。

entries.definition: The ordinary English noun of entering, from the same French stem.
entries.definitionCN: 英语中表进入的普通名词，与它同词干。

entries.definition: An idiom of chain restaurants, where the phrase sits beside a list of plates.
entries.definitionCN: 连锁餐馆的说法，指与主菜并列的项。

entries.definition: The starter in British usage, which overlaps the older sense of the word.
entries.definitionCN: 英式头盘，与该词的旧义部分重叠。

entries.definition: The unambiguous British name for the central dish.
entries.definitionCN: 英式对主盘不含混的说法。

entries.definition: The first plate in British menus, matching the older entree sense.
entries.definitionCN: 英式菜单的第一盘，对应旧义。

entries.definition: A route into a field, used in the figurative sense.
entries.definitionCN: 进入某领域的路径，用于比喻义。

entries.definition: A position secured inside a group, as in get a footing.
entries.definitionCN: 在群体中站稳的位置，如 get a footing。

normalIntro.en: Think of a door: the American reading is the dish that enters the table, and the figurative reading is the door itself.
normalIntro.cn: 把词想成一扇门：美式指登上桌的菜，比喻义就是门本身。

normal.en: In the United States the entree is the main plate.
normal.cn: 在美国，entree 指主盘。

normal.en: In Britain it can mean the course that comes first.
normal.cn: 在英国它可指最先上的那道。

normal.en: Say an entree into a field for the access sense.
normal.cn: 表进入某领域时说 an entree into a field。

normal.en: Menus keep the accent mark in formal writing.
normal.cn: 正式菜单书写常保留重音符号。

normal.en: Do not spell it envelope; the ending is the same as in entry.
normal.cn: 不要拼作 envelope；词尾与 entry 相同。

abstract.en: Picture a waiter lifting a cover off the central plate.
abstract.cn: 想象侍者揭开中间餐盘的盖。

abstract.en: Imagine the first page of a menu turning itself.
abstract.cn: 想象菜单第一页自己翻动。

abstract.en: Think of a card that admits you through a side door.
abstract.cn: 想想一张带你走侧门入场的卡。

examples.en: The restaurant lists three entrees and six sides.
examples.cn: 这家餐厅列出三道主菜与六种配菜。

examples.en: Fluent French was her entree into diplomacy.
examples.cn: 流利的法语是她进入外交界的门径。

examples.en: A tasting entree arrives in small bowls.
examples.cn: 一份试味头盘用小碗端上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺来」——音近 entree，菜端上来时说俺来了，所以是主菜或头盘；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 intrare（进入）→ 古法语 entrer／entrée → 英语 entree，核心义「进入；登桌的首盘」，与 entry 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The noun names a dish by its place in the meal and, by transfer, a person's place at the door of a career.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词按菜品在餐席中的位置命名，并由此转移到人在职业门口的位子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the thing that comes in first, whether a plate or a person.
core.cn: 核心意象：最先入席者，无论是一盘菜还是一位客人。

branches.en: American menus fix the word on the central dish.
branches.cn: 美式菜单把词固定在中间那道。

branches.en: Older usage keeps it at the opening of the meal.
branches.cn: 较早用法把它留在开席位置。

branches.en: The door image transfers the word to professions.
branches.cn: 门的意象把词转移到职业领域。

branches.en: Both readings are menu positions that vary by country.
branches.cn: 两义都是随地区不同的菜单位置。

branches.en: Being first in and being let in share one idea.
branches.cn: 先入席与被放入共享同一概念。

intro.en: A Latin prefix of inward motion plus a French nominal ending forms this borrowed noun.
intro.cn: 拉丁语表向内的前缀加法语名词词尾构成这个借入名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin In means into and intra means within; intrare is the verb of going in.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in 表向内，intra 表在内，intrare 是进入的动词。

items.meaning: a door or the right to enter

items.example: The old term survives in menus.

definition_zh: 创业者；企业家；承担风险创办事业的人
definition_en: a person who starts a business and takes on the financial risk in order to make a profit
core_image: 一个人把全部积蓄换成一台机器，机器的开关还没按下
scene: 那位年轻创业者把全部积蓄投进一台新烘干机，开了一家自助洗衣店。The young entrepreneur put her entire savings into a new drying machine and opened a self-service laundry.
sceneCN: 那位年轻创业者把全部积蓄投进一台新烘干机，开了一家自助洗衣店；句中的 entrepreneur 指「自己出资创办事业并承担风险的人」（第 1 个义项：创办新事业的人）。图中可辨识物件：烘干机、投币盒、洗衣篮、租约。

forms.label: 相关名词（创业活动、创业精神）

senses.title: Someone who starts a venture
senses.definition: a person who sets up a new business, usually committing their own money and effort
senses.definitionCN: 创办新企业的人，通常投入自己的钱与精力
senses.example: The young entrepreneur put her entire savings into a new drying machine and opened a self-service laundry.
senses.exampleCN: 那位年轻创业者把全部积蓄投进一台新烘干机，开了一家自助洗衣店。
senses.why: The French source means 'one who undertakes', so the word names the person who takes a venture in hand.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源意为「承担者」，因此这个词指把事业接到手里的人。

senses.title: An organizer of the factors of production
senses.titleCN: 组织生产要素的企业家
senses.definition: in economics, the person who combines capital, labour and materials into a working business
senses.definitionCN: 经济学上把资本、劳动与原料组合成可运转企业的人
senses.example: The textbook defines the entrepreneur as the one who coordinates land, labour and capital.
senses.exampleCN: 教科书把企业家定义为协调土地、劳动与资本的人。
senses.why: Classical economics needed a name for the agent who assembles the other inputs, and borrowed this French word for it.
senses.whyCN: 古典经济学需要为「把其他要素组合起来的人」起个名字，就借用了这个法语词。

senses.title: A self-employed owner-operator
senses.definition: a person who runs their own small business and earns from it rather than from a wage
senses.definitionCN: 经营自己的小企业、靠经营所得而非工资生活的人
senses.example: Many entrepreneurs in the town run one-person workshops.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上许多创业者经营只有一个人的作坊。
senses.why: Owning the venture and working in it are one act for a small operator, so the word covers the self-employed.
senses.whyCN: 对小经营者来说，拥有事业与在其中劳作是同一件事，因此这个词涵盖自雇者。

senses.title: The bearer of business risk
senses.definition: the party who risks their own capital on an uncertain outcome and keeps the residual gain or loss
senses.definitionCN: 把自有资本押在不确定结果上、并承担剩余盈亏的一方
senses.example: The entrepreneur bears the loss if the shop fails.
senses.exampleCN: 如果店铺失败，损失由创业者承担。
senses.why: Undertaking includes taking the downside, so risk bearing became the defining economic mark of the word.
senses.whyCN: 「承担」本来就包含承担坏结果，因此负险成了这个词在经济上的标志。

senses.title: An innovator who breaks old routines
senses.definition: a person who introduces a new product, method or market and displaces established ways of doing things
senses.definitionCN: 引入新产品、新方法或新市场，取代既有做法的人
senses.example: Schumpeter treated the entrepreneur as the force that destroyed old combinations.
senses.exampleCN: 熊彼特把企业家看作摧毁旧组合的力量。
senses.why: Innovation is a form of undertaking: the new combination has to be carried through against existing habits.
senses.whyCN: 创新是承担的一种形态：新的组合必须顶着既有习惯被推行到底。

senses.title: A contractor or promoter of a project
senses.definition: a person who takes on and organizes a specific project, such as a public work or an entertainment
senses.definitionCN: 承接并组织某个具体项目的人，如公共工程或演出
senses.example: The entrepreneur behind the festival booked the whole square.
senses.exampleCN: 操办这个节庆的承办人把整个广场都订下了。
senses.why: The word entered English for the promoter of a musical or theatrical production, and this project sense survives.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初进入英语时指音乐或戏剧演出的承办人，这一项目义保留至今。

senses.title: A repeat founder
senses.definition: a person who starts one venture after another, often selling each before beginning the next
senses.definitionCN: 接连创办事业、常在开始下一个之前卖掉前一个的人
senses.example: The serial entrepreneur had sold three companies by forty.
senses.exampleCN: 这位连续创业者到四十岁时已经卖掉了三家公司。
senses.why: If starting is the core act, repeating it becomes a recognisable type of person.
senses.whyCN: 如果创办是核心动作，反复做这个动作就成为一种可辨认的人。

senses.title: A calculated gambler in business
senses.titleCN: 敢于下注的商界冒险者
senses.definition: a person who commits heavily to an uncertain commercial bet, admired or blamed for boldness
senses.definitionCN: 把大量资源押在不确定的商业赌注上、因大胆而被赞赏或指责的人
senses.example: The entrepreneur staked the factory on a single export contract.
senses.exampleCN: 这位冒险者把整座工厂押在一份出口合同上。
senses.why: Risk bearing pushed to its extreme looks like gambling, and the word takes on that colour in everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 把负险推到极端就像赌博，这个词在日常说法里就带上了这层色彩。

intro.en: Entrepreneur is French for 'one who undertakes', from entreprendre 'to take in hand'. English borrowed it in the eighteenth century for a promoter of entertainments, and economics gave it its modern sense in the nineteenth. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: entrepreneur 是法语「承担者」，出自 entreprendre「着手、承担」。英语在十八世纪借入，指演出承办人；经济学在十九世纪赋予它现代含义。年代均为约数。

items.en: Entreprendre 'to undertake' joined a prefix meaning 'between' with prendre 'to take', itself from Latin prehendere 'to grasp'.
items.cn: entreprendre「承担」把意为「之间」的前缀与 prendre「拿取」结合，后者出自拉丁 prehendere「抓住」。

items.en: Entrepreneur named the person who undertakes a task, with no necessary link to trade or profit.
items.cn: entrepreneur 指承担某项任务的人，与买卖或利润没有必然联系。

items.en: English used entrepreneur first for someone who organized public entertainments, especially musical or theatrical productions.
items.cn: 英语最初用 entrepreneur 指组织公共演出的人，尤其是音乐或戏剧制作。

items.en: Nineteenth-century economists, notably Jean-Baptiste Say, made the word mean the agent who combines production and bears the risk.
items.cn: 十九世纪的经济学家，尤其是萨伊，使这个词指组合生产并承担风险的主体。

items.en: Schumpeter shifted the emphasis from mere ownership to innovation, and that reading dominates business writing today.
items.cn: 熊彼特把重点从单纯的所有权转到创新，这一读法如今主导商业写作。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same taking root; group two holds names for people who run or start businesses.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「拿取」词根的词；第二组是经营或创办企业者的称呼。

entries.definition: The undertaking itself, whether a firm or a project; entrepreneur is the person who carries it.
entries.definitionCN: 指被承担的事业本身，无论企业或项目；entrepreneur 是承担它的人。

entries.definition: An adjective describing the outlook or style of such a person, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述这类人的眼光或风格，不指人本身。

entries.definition: The activity or skill of starting ventures; the noun names the practice, not the practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 指创办事业的活动或本领；命名的是实践，不是实践者。

entries.definition: A person who acts like a founder inside an existing company; the prefix marks the setting.
entries.definitionCN: 指在现有公司内部像创办者那样行事的人；前缀标明了场景。

entries.definition: A person who establishes an organization; it records the act of setting up, not the ongoing risk.
entries.definitionCN: 指建立某个组织的人；记录的是创立动作，不是持续承担的风险。

entries.definition: A man engaged in trade; it does not require that he started the firm or bears its risk.
entries.definitionCN: 指从事买卖的男子；不要求他创办企业或承担其风险。

entries.definition: An owner or manager of large manufacturing enterprises; grander and narrower than entrepreneur.
entries.definitionCN: 指大型制造企业的所有者或管理者；比 entrepreneur 更宏大也更窄。

entries.definition: A promoter of concerts, theatre or opera; it keeps the older English sense of entrepreneur.
entries.definitionCN: 指音乐会、戏剧或歌剧的承办人；保留了 entrepreneur 在英语中较旧的意义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: French for 'one who undertakes': the person who takes the venture in hand.
normal.cn: 法语意为「承担者」：把事业接到手里的人。

normal.en: The family runs entrepreneur, entrepreneurs, entrepreneurial and entrepreneurship.
normal.cn: 同族词有 entrepreneur、entrepreneurs、entrepreneurial 与 entrepreneurship。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the types: a young entrepreneur, a serial entrepreneur, a social entrepreneur.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出类型：年轻创业者、连续创业者、社会创业者。

normal.en: The same root gives enterprise for the venture and entrepreneur for the person.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 enterprise（事业）与 entrepreneur（承担者）。

normal.en: Economics added the risk-bearing sense; innovation writing added the disruptive sense.
normal.cn: 经济学加上负险义，创新论述又加上颠覆义。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing on a heavy lever before anyone knows whether it will move.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手握住一根重杠杆，还没人知道它会不会动。

abstract.en: Picture a savings jar emptied in one motion onto a workbench.
abstract.cn: 想象一只存钱罐被一次性倒空在作台上。

abstract.en: Picture a map with one route drawn and all the others left blank.
abstract.cn: 想象一张只画了一条路线、其余都空着的地图。

examples.en: The city offers cheap office space to young entrepreneurs.
examples.cn: 该市向年轻创业者提供廉价办公空间。

examples.en: An entrepreneur must accept that most attempts fail.
examples.cn: 创业者必须接受大多数尝试会失败。

examples.en: The entrepreneur sold the company and started a second one.
examples.cn: 这位创业者卖掉公司后又创办了第二家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把存钱罐倒空在作台上，旁边是一台新机器 → 创业者

root: 法语 entrepreneur「承担者」，出自 entreprendre「着手、承担」= entre-「之间」+ prendre「拿取」，后者出自拉丁 prehendere「抓住」；英语十八世纪借入，十九世纪由经济学固定为「承担风险创办事业的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one person taking a venture in hand: the founder, the organizer of production, the self-employed operator, the risk bearer, the innovator, the project promoter, the repeat founder, and the bold gambler.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个把事业接到手里的人：创办者、生产组织者、自雇经营者、风险承担者、创新者、项目承办人、连续创业者，以及大胆下注的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person emptying a savings jar onto a workbench beside a new machine.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人把存钱罐倒空在作台上，旁边是一台新机器。

branches.en: TAKING IT ON: founding a venture and running it alone are the same act at different sizes.
branches.cn: 接下事业：创办企业与独自经营，是同一动作的不同规模。

branches.en: ORGANIZER: economics turns the undertaker into the agent who assembles land, labour and capital.
branches.cn: 组织者：经济学把承担者变成组合土地、劳动与资本的主体。

branches.en: BET: bearing the downside and staking everything are the same risk at different temperatures.
branches.cn: 赌注：承担坏结果与押上全部，是同一风险的两种温度。

branches.en: INNOVATOR: the new combination must be carried through against old habits.
branches.cn: 创新者：新的组合必须顶着旧习惯被推行到底。

branches.en: REPEATED UNDERTAKING: a promoter of shows and a repeat founder both take project after project in hand.
branches.cn: 反复承担：演出承办人与连续创业者，都一件接一件地把项目接到手里。

intro.en: Entrepreneur is a French agent noun built from a taking verb; its English family supplies the adjective and the practice noun.
intro.cn: entrepreneur 是由「拿取」动词构成的法语施事名词；英语词族给出形容词与实践名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin prehendere gives prehensile and comprehend; French entreprendre gives entrepreneur, enterprise and enterprising.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 prehendere 给出 prehensile 与 comprehend；法语 entreprendre 给出 entrepreneur、enterprise 与 enterprising。

items.example: The root pictures a hand closing on a tool.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根描绘一只手合拢抓住工具。

items.example: The verb means to take a task in hand.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词意为把任务接到手里。
这位创业者开了那家洗衣店。
十位创业者加入了这项计划。

items.meaningCN: 与创业者和创业有关的
items.example: The city has an entrepreneurial culture.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市有一种创业文化。

items.meaningCN: 创办事业的实践与本领
items.example: Entrepreneurship is now taught at school.
items.exampleCN: 创业如今在学校里教授。
这笔资金被以创业的方式使用。

items.meaning: a founder-type figure inside a firm
items.example: An intrapreneur built the new unit.
items.exampleCN: 一位机构内创业者组建了新部门。

latinEntries.meaning: to seize, grasp, take hold of

definition_zh: 创业的；有创业精神的；企业家式的；敢冒风险开创新事的
definition_en: relating to someone who starts businesses, or showing the initiative and risk-taking of such a person
core_image: 一间公司里，几个人把旧流程撕下，换上自己画的新流程图
scene: 创业氛围浓厚的园区里，她把团队拆成小组快速试错。Entrepreneurial staff volunteered to run the pilot quickly.
sceneCN: 她把公司里最敢试错的一组人单独拉出来做新项目；句中的 entrepreneurial 指「具有主动开创与试错精神的」（第 2 个义项：具有创业精神的）。图中可辨识物件：新流程图、白板、旧流程纸、项目挂牌。

pos.zh: 创业的；有创业精神的；企业家式的；敢冒风险的

senses.title: Relating to people who start businesses
senses.titleCN: 创业的；与创办企业有关的
senses.definition: connected with entrepreneurs or with the founding of new businesses
senses.definitionCN: 与创业者或与新企业创办有关的
senses.example: The city runs an entrepreneurial grant for first-time founders.
senses.exampleCN: 该市为首次创办者提供一笔创业补助。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the person to a noun, saying that the thing belongs to the world of founders.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把那个人挂到名词上，说明所指数事物属于创办者的世界。

senses.title: Showing initiative and willingness to try
senses.titleCN: 具有主动开创与试错精神的
senses.definition: showing the drive to begin new things and to try methods that may fail
senses.definitionCN: 表现出启动新事、并尝试可能失败的方法的劲头
senses.example: She pulled the most entrepreneurial team in the company out to run a new project.
senses.exampleCN: 她把公司里最敢试错的一组人单独拉出来做新项目。
senses.why: The person noun carries the drive to undertake, and the adjective transfers that drive onto a team or a attitude.
senses.whyCN: 指人的名词本身带着「承担」的劲头，形容词把这种劲头转移到团队或态度上。

senses.title: Businesslike in a creative, deal-making way
senses.titleCN: 企业家式的；善于经营与撮合的
senses.definition: acting with the resourcefulness and deal-making skill associated with business owners
senses.definitionCN: 以企业主那种善找资源、善撮合交易的方式行事
senses.example: He took an entrepreneurial approach to the empty warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 他以企业家式的办法处理那间空仓库。
senses.why: Owners must find money, partners and customers at once, and the adjective names that combined knack.
senses.whyCN: 企业主必须同时找钱、找伙伴、找客户，这个形容词命名的是这种综合本事。

senses.title: Ready to accept financial risk
senses.definition: willing to commit money or resources to an uncertain outcome
senses.definitionCN: 愿意把钱或资源押在不确定结果上的
senses.example: Their entrepreneurial bet on the new line almost failed.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在新产线上的冒险押注几乎失败。
senses.why: Risk bearing is the economic core of the founder, and the adjective marks that readiness.
senses.whyCN: 承担风险是创办者在经济上的核心，这个形容词标记的就是这种准备。

senses.title: Enterprising and full of drive
senses.definition: energetic and eager to seize opportunities rather than wait for instruction
senses.definitionCN: 有精力、急于抓住机会，而不是等别人吩咐
senses.example: The most entrepreneurial students ran the market stall themselves.
senses.exampleCN: 最有闯劲的学生自己操办了集市摊位。
senses.why: If the practice is undertaking, the adjective also describes the temperament that undertakes readily.
senses.whyCN: 如果这种实践是「承担」，这个形容词也描述那种乐于承担的性格。

senses.title: Given freedom to act like an owner
senses.titleCN: 被赋予自主开拓空间的（团队、岗位）
senses.definition: describing a role or unit that is allowed to experiment and decide without close supervision
senses.definitionCN: 描述被允许试验、无须紧密监督即可决定的岗位或单元
senses.example: The firm created an entrepreneurial unit with its own budget.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司设立了一个拥有独立预算的自主开拓单元。
senses.why: Firms borrow the founder's freedom for selected teams, and the adjective marks that granted autonomy.
senses.whyCN: 公司把创办者的自由借给特定团队，这个形容词标记的是被授予的自主。

senses.title: Describing an economy or culture of founders
senses.titleCN: 创业型的（经济、文化、地区）
senses.definition: used of an economy, region or culture in which starting businesses is common and valued
senses.definitionCN: 用于创办企业普遍且受重视的经济、地区或文化
senses.example: The province developed an entrepreneurial economy after the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 改革之后，该省发展出一种创业型经济。
senses.why: Many founders acting at once create a climate, and the adjective can describe that climate.
senses.whyCN: 许多创办者同时行动会形成一种气候，这个形容词也用来描述那种气候。

senses.title: Quick to spot an opportunity
senses.definition: skilled at noticing an unmet need and turning it into a commercial opening
senses.definitionCN: 擅长察觉未被满足的需求并把它变成商业机会
senses.example: Her entrepreneurial eye noticed the queue nobody was serving.
senses.exampleCN: 她那种善于发现机会的眼光注意到没人服务的队伍。
senses.why: Opportunity is the raw material a founder works with, so the adjective also names the ability to see it.
senses.whyCN: 机会是创办者的原料，因此这个形容词也命名看见它的能力。

intro.en: Entrepreneurial is entrepreneur plus the adjectival suffix -ial, from Latin -alis. English built the adjective in the nineteenth century alongside the economic sense of the noun. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: entrepreneurial 是 entrepreneur 加上形容词后缀 -ial 构成，后者出自拉丁 -alis。英语在十九世纪随名词的经济义一同造出这个形容词。年代均为约数。

items.en: The base verb meant 'to take in hand, undertake', built on Latin prehendere 'to grasp'.
items.cn: 基础动词意为「着手、承担」，由拉丁 prehendere「抓住」构成。

items.en: The person noun named one who undertakes a venture, and English borrowed it in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 指人的名词指承担事业者，英语在十八世纪借入。

items.en: The suffix -alis formed adjectives of relation in Latin and became -al and -ial in English, as in financial and commercial.
items.cn: 后缀 -alis 在拉丁语中构成关系形容词，在英语中变成 -al 与 -ial，如 financial 与 commercial。

items.en: Economists needed an adjective for the new noun, and entrepreneurial appeared to describe ventures, risk and behaviour.
items.cn: 经济学家需要为这个新名词配一个形容词，entrepreneurial 遂出现，描述事业、风险与行为。

items.en: Twentieth-century management writing extended it to teams, units and whole cultures, widening its range.
items.cn: 二十世纪的管理写作把它扩展到团队、单元与整体文化，拓宽了它的范围。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same word; group two holds adjectives for similar temperaments.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词的各种形式；第二组是描述相近性情的形容词。

entries.definition: The founder himself or herself; the adjective describes the quality rather than the person.
entries.definitionCN: 指创办者本人；形容词描述的是性质，不是人。

entries.definition: The activity or field; the adjective cannot replace it as the subject of a course.
entries.definitionCN: 指活动或领域；形容词不能替代它作课程的科目名。

entries.definition: An older adjective meaning full of initiative, without the economic and risk-bearing weight of entrepreneurial.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的形容词，指富有主动性，没有 entrepreneurial 的经济与负险分量。

entries.definition: The same adjective applied to founder-like behaviour inside an existing organization.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词，用于既有组织内部类似创办者的行为。

entries.definition: Introducing new ideas or methods; it stresses novelty, not ownership or financial risk.
entries.definitionCN: 指引入新想法或方法；强调新颖，不强调所有权或财务风险。

entries.definition: Acting in advance rather than reacting; it describes timing, while entrepreneurial describes outlook.
entries.definitionCN: 指提前行动而非被动反应；描述时机，entrepreneurial 描述眼光。

entries.definition: Willing to take risks, often physical ones; narrower and more hazardous in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 指愿意冒险，常指身体上的风险；范围更窄，语气更危险。

entries.definition: Eager for success and achievement; it may lack the commercial and experimental colour.
entries.definitionCN: 指渴望成功与成就；可能缺少商业与试验的色彩。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Entrepreneur plus the relating suffix: belonging to the founder's world.
normal.cn: entrepreneur 加关系后缀：属于创办者的世界。

normal.en: The family runs entrepreneur, entrepreneurial, entrepreneurship and intrapreneurial.
normal.cn: 同族词有 entrepreneur、entrepreneurial、entrepreneurship 与 intrapreneurial。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: an entrepreneurial culture, entrepreneurial skills, entrepreneurial spirit.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出各义项：创业文化、创业技能、创业精神。

normal.en: The Latin relating suffix also builds financial and commercial.
normal.cn: 同一拉丁关系后缀还构成 financial 与 commercial。

normal.en: Management writing applies it to units and budgets, not only to people.
normal.cn: 管理写作把它用到单元与预算上，不只用于人。

abstract.en: Picture an old flow chart torn off a wall and a hand-drawn one pinned in its place.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上一张旧流程图被撕下，一张手绘的钉在原来的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a locked room with one key left on the table for whoever dares to use it.
abstract.cn: 想象一间上锁的房间，桌上留着一把钥匙，谁敢用就归谁。

abstract.en: Picture a queue nobody serves, and one person already setting up a stall beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条没人招呼的队伍，旁边已有人支起了摊子。

examples.en: The programme gives small loans to entrepreneurial women.
examples.cn: 该项目向有创业精神的女性提供小额贷款。

examples.en: An entrepreneurial manager tested the new service in one branch.
examples.cn: 一位有闯劲的经理在一家分行试行了新服务。

examples.en: The region's entrepreneurial culture attracts outside investors.
examples.cn: 该地区的创业文化吸引了外来投资者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 旧流程图被撕下，手绘的新图钉上墙 → 有闯劲的

root: 英语构词：entrepreneur（法语「承担者」，出自拉丁 prehendere「抓住」）+ 拉丁关系后缀 -alis（英语作 -ial）；指与创办事业或创业者有关的性质。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective: belonging to founders, showing initiative, businesslike resourcefulness, accepting risk, enterprising, granted autonomy, describing a regional culture, and spotting opportunity.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个形容词：属于创办者、显出主动性、善于撮合资源、接受风险、有闯劲、被赋予自主、描述地区文化，以及善于发现机会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old flow chart torn down and a hand-drawn one pinned up.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧流程图被撕下，手绘的新图钉了上去。

branches.en: BELONGING TO FOUNDERS: one firm's adjective and a whole region's climate describe the same world at different scales.
branches.cn: 属于创办者：一家企业的形容词与整个地区的气候，是同一世界的两种尺度。

branches.en: DRIVE: willingness to begin and readiness to seize an occasion are one temperament.
branches.cn: 闯劲：愿意开始与急于抓住时机，是同一种性情。

branches.en: RESOURCEFUL: finding money, partners and customers at once is the founder's knack.
branches.cn: 善找资源：同时找钱、找伙伴与找客户，是创办者的本事。

branches.en: RISK: committing money to an uncertain outcome is the economic core.
branches.cn: 风险：把钱押在不确定结果上，是经济上的核心。

branches.en: GRANTED FREEDOM: a team allowed to act like an owner is expected to notice what others miss.
branches.cn: 被授予自由：被允许像业主那样行动的团队，被期待看见别人漏掉的东西。

intro.en: Entrepreneurial is a French agent noun plus a Latin relating suffix, a very common English pattern.
intro.cn: entrepreneurial 是法语施事名词加拉丁关系后缀，是英语中极常见的模式。

latinIntro.en: Latin prehendere supplies the root; Latin -alis supplies the suffix seen in financial, commercial and manual.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 prehendere 提供词根；拉丁 -alis 提供后缀，见于 financial、commercial 与 manual。

items.example: The root pictures a hand closing on a task.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根描绘一只手合拢抓住任务。

items.example: The verb means to take a task in hand.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词意为把任务接到手里。
这位创业者开了那家店。

items.example: The team had an entrepreneurial style.

items.exampleCN: 这笔资金被以创业的方式使用。

items.meaningCN: 在企业内部像创办者那样的
items.example: The unit was given an intrapreneurial budget.
items.exampleCN: 该单元获得了机构内创业预算。

definition_zh: 委托；托付；交付
definition_en: to give someone a task or a valuable thing and rely on them to take care of it
core_image: 把手里的钥匙和一份文件一起放到对方掌心，然后松开手指
scene: 老经理把新客户的档案交给她跟进。The senior manager entrusted her with the new accounts.
sceneCN: 这里 entrust 是「委托；托付」（第 1 个义项：交付任务并依赖对方照管）；句意：资深经理把新客户档案托付给她。

senses.title: To hand a task to someone reliable
senses.definition: to give a piece of work to a person because you believe they will do it well
senses.definitionCN: 因相信对方能做好而把工作交给他们
senses.example: The director entrusted the audit to a junior partner.
senses.exampleCN: 总监把审计工作交给一位初级合伙人。
senses.why: The prefix en- puts a thing into the state of trust, so the verb always carries reliance.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 en- 把事物放入 trust 的状态，因此动词总含依赖之意。

senses.title: To give a valuable item for safekeeping
senses.definition: to leave a valuable or sensitive thing in another person's care
senses.definitionCN: 把贵重或敏感之物交由他人照管
senses.example: She entrusted her savings to the family solicitor.
senses.exampleCN: 她把积蓄交给家族法律顾问保管。
senses.why: Applied to objects, the verb keeps the same two-part relation of giver and keeper.
senses.whyCN: 用于物品时，动词保留给予者与保管者之间的同一双重关系。

senses.title: To commit an outcome to chance or principle
senses.definition: to leave a result in the hands of an impersonal force such as fate or the market
senses.definitionCN: 把结果交由命运或市场之类非人的力量决定
senses.example: He entrusted his future to no one but himself.
senses.exampleCN: 他不把前途交给任何人，只靠自己。
senses.why: Abstract uses extend the same structure beyond people and objects.
senses.whyCN: 抽象用法把同一结构延伸到他人与物品之外。

intro.en: Entrust joins en- to trust, whose stem came into English from Old Norse rather than French.
intro.cn: entrust 由 en- 加 trust 构成，而 trust 的词干来自古诺斯语而非法语。

items.en: Traust means confidence or security.
items.cn: traust 意为信赖与保障。

items.en: Trust appears first as a noun of safety.
items.cn: 中古英语中 trust 先作保障义的名词。

items.en: Entrust is recorded with the sense of committing to care.
items.cn: 近代早期英语记录 entrust，表交付照管。

items.en: Commercial letters use the verb for shipped goods.
items.cn: 十七世纪商业信件用它指发运货物。

items.en: Legal English prefers entrust in fiduciary contexts.
items.cn: 现代法律英语在受托责任语境中更用 entrust。

note.en: Group one holds the trust family; group two holds other verbs of handing over.
note.cn: 第一组是 trust 同族词；第二组是其他交付类动词。

entries.definition: The stem word, which names both confidence and a legal holding of property.
entries.definitionCN: 词基本词，兼指信任与依法持有财产。

entries.definition: The participle and past form, frequent in passive reporting.
entries.definitionCN: 分词与过去式，常见于被动报道。

entries.definition: The action noun, chiefly in legal drafting.
entries.definitionCN: 动作名词，主要用于法律文书。

entries.definition: Same stem with a prefix of separation, naming the loss of reliance.
entries.definitionCN: 同词干加表分离的前缀，指失去信赖。

entries.definition: To share secrets or responsibilities relying on the listener's discretion.
entries.definitionCN: 倚重对方守密而分享秘密或责任。

entries.definition: To pass on duties with the power to act, more formal in workplaces.
entries.definitionCN: 连同权力移交职责，职场上更正式。

entries.definition: To hand something over for care, as in commit a child to a school.
entries.definitionCN: 交付照管，如把孩子送入学校。

entries.definition: To give out tasks by rule rather than by personal reliance.
entries.definitionCN: 按规则分配任务，而非倚重私人信任。

normalIntro.en: Entrust is en plus trust, so every use involves one party relying on another.
normalIntro.cn: entrust 是 en 加 trust，因此每种用法都含一方倚重另一方。

normal.en: Two patterns: entrust somebody with a thing, entrust a thing to somebody.
normal.cn: 两种句型：把物托给某人，或把某物交予某人。

normal.en: The person is the object in the first pattern, the thing in the second.
normal.cn: 前一句型以人为宾语，后一句型以物为宾语。

normal.en: Passive voice keeps the thing as subject: the files were entrusted to her.
normal.cn: 被动式让物作主语：文件被交给她。

normal.en: It implies risk, so exams pair it with care, safekeeping, and duty.
normal.cn: 词义含风险，故常与照管、保管、责任同现。

normal.en: Do not confuse entrust with intrust, an older variant rarely printed now.
normal.cn: 不要与 intrust 混淆，那是今已少见的旧变体。

abstract.en: Picture two hands meeting over a set of keys.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手在一串钥匙上方相叠。

abstract.en: Imagine a sealed envelope crossing a counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一只封口的信封越过柜台。

abstract.en: Think of a lifeguard taking over the whistle mid-shift.
abstract.cn: 想想救生员在轮班中途接过哨子。

examples.en: They entrusted the archive to a university library.
examples.cn: 他们把档案托付给一所大学图书馆。

examples.en: Her parents entrusted her with the house keys.
examples.cn: 父母把家钥匙交给她保管。

examples.en: The mission was entrusted to the youngest team.
examples.cn: 这项任务交给了最年轻的小组。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因他存」——因为他在，东西才交给他存放，所以 entrust 是托付；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古诺斯语 traust（信赖、保障）→ 中古英语 trust＋前缀 en-（使入）→ 近代英语 entrust，核心义「交付给对方保管」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb covers handing over work, handing over valuables, and committing outcomes to impersonal forces.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词涵盖移交工作、移交贵重物，以及把结果交给非人的力量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fingers opening to release an object into another palm.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指松开，把物件放入另一只掌心。

branches.en: Work passes to whoever can be relied upon.
branches.cn: 工作交给可倚重之人。

branches.en: Valuables pass into someone's safekeeping.
branches.cn: 贵重物交由他人保管。

branches.en: Abstract outcomes pass to chance or principle.
branches.cn: 抽象结果交由命运或原则。

branches.en: Both need a keeper who accepts the duty.
branches.cn: 两者都需要接受责任的保管者。

branches.en: Trust is the common thread in objects and hopes.
branches.cn: 信任是物品与期望共通的线。

intro.en: An English prefix joins a Norse-derived stem, and the family grows with legal endings.
intro.cn: 英语前缀接古诺斯语来源的词干，词族由法律词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Legal Latin written as fides means faith and credits names the trust of a creditor.
latinIntro.cn: 法律拉丁语 fides 表信义，credits 指债权人的信托关系。

items.exampleCN: en- 位于 entrust 开头。

items.meaning: a person holding property in trust

definition_zh: 入口；条目；参赛作品；进入
definition_en: a way in, an item in a list, or a thing entered in a competition
core_image: 一扇门通向里面的房间，门边还挂着一块记录牌
scene: 博物馆的侧门只对工作人员开放。The side entry of the museum is open only to staff.
sceneCN: 这里 entry 是「入口」（第 1 个义项：进入的通道或门）；句意：博物馆的侧门只对工作人员开放。

pos.zh: 入口；条目；参赛作品；进入

senses.title: A way in
senses.definition: a door, gate, or passage through which one enters
senses.definitionCN: 供人进入的门、大门或通道
senses.example: The side entry was blocked by boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 侧面的入口被箱子堵住了。
senses.why: Entry first names the act of going in, and then the place where that act happens.
senses.whyCN: entry 最初指进入的动作，随后指发生这一动作的地方。

senses.title: An item in a list or record
senses.definition: a single item written in a list, diary, dictionary, or record
senses.definitionCN: 写在清单、日记、词典或记录中的单项
senses.example: He wrote a short entry in his diary.
senses.exampleCN: 他在日记里写了一条简短的记录。
senses.why: What is entered into a book becomes an entry, so the word names one recorded item.
senses.whyCN: 被写进书里的内容成为 entry，因此这个词指一条被记录的项目。

senses.title: A competition submission
senses.definition: a person or work entered in a competition
senses.definitionCN: 报名参加比赛的人或作品
senses.example: Her entry won the photography prize.
senses.exampleCN: 她的参赛作品赢得了摄影奖。
senses.why: To enter a contest is to put something in, and the thing put in is the entry.
senses.whyCN: 参加比赛就是把某物投进去，被投进去的东西就是 entry。

senses.title: The act of entering
senses.definition: the act of going into a place, group, or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 进入某地、加入某团体或协定的行为
senses.example: The country's entry into the trade agreement took years.
senses.exampleCN: 该国加入这项贸易协定花了好几年。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply the act of going in, which still appears in formal phrases.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义就是进入的动作，这一含义仍出现在正式短语中。

intro.en: Entry comes from Latin intrare, to enter, through Old French entree, and it keeps both the act and the place of entering.
intro.cn: entry 来自拉丁语 intrare（进入），经古法语 entree 进入英语，同时保留「进入的动作」与「进入之处」两层含义。

items.en: Intrare means to go in or enter.
items.cn: intrare 意为走进去、进入。

items.en: Intro means within or inside.
items.cn: intro 意为在内部。

items.en: Entree names both the act and the place of entering.
items.cn: entree 同时指进入的动作和进入的地点。

items.en: Entry appears with the same double sense.
items.cn: 中古英语 entry 出现时也带有这双重含义。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of a recorded item.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「记录条目」的含义。

note.en: Entry is a going-in word and a record word, so it sits near enter words and near words for access.
note.cn: entry 既表示「进入」，也表示「记录」，因此与 enter 词族及表示通行的词相邻。

entries.definition: to go into a place
entries.definitionCN: 进入

entries.definition: a way in or the act of entering
entries.definitionCN: 入口；进入

entries.definition: a person who enters
entries.definitionCN: 进入者；参赛者

entries.definition: a door or passage for entering
entries.definitionCN: 入口；通道

entries.definition: the right or way to enter
entries.definitionCN: 进入权；通道

entries.definition: permission or payment to enter
entries.definitionCN: 准许进入；入场

normalIntro.en: Entry is the noun of enter: the way in, the act of going in, or the thing you put into a list.
normalIntro.cn: entry 是 enter 的名词：进去的路、进去的动作，或你写进清单里的那一项。

normal.en: No entry means you may not go in.
normal.cn: no entry 表示禁止进入。

normal.en: A dictionary entry is one word and its explanation.
normal.cn: dictionary entry 是一个词及其解释。

normal.en: An entry form is the paper you fill in to join.
normal.cn: entry form 是报名时填写的表格。

normal.en: The plural entries covers lists and contestants alike.
normal.cn: 复数 entries 既可指多条记录，也可指多位参赛者。

normal.en: Compare entrance: entrance stresses the doorway, entry suits records and contests too.
normal.cn: 对比 entrance：entrance 强调门口，entry 还适用于记录和比赛。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow gate with a small sign beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇窄门，旁边挂着一块小牌子。

abstract.en: Imagine a line written neatly in a notebook.
abstract.cn: 想象笔记本上工整地写着一行字。

abstract.en: Think of a sealed box waiting on a contest table.
abstract.cn: 想象一个封好的盒子放在比赛桌上等待评审。

examples.en: The back entry leads to a small garden.
examples.cn: 后门通向一个小花园。

examples.en: Each entry in the list has a date.
examples.cn: 清单上的每一条记录都有一个日期。

examples.en: The judges praised the youngest entry.
examples.cn: 评委称赞了最年轻的参赛作品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en + try」——想进去就得试一试；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 intrare（进入）→ 古法语 entree（进入；入口）→ 中古英语 entry，核心义「进入」，引申为入口与记录条目。

sensesIntro.en: Entry begins with the act of going in, then names the place, the recorded item, and the thing submitted to a contest.
sensesIntro.cn: entry 从进入的动作开始，随后指进入之处、被记录的项目以及提交参赛的作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doorway, with a ledger open nearby.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇门，旁边摊开一本登记簿。

branches.en: The doorway is the place of entering.
branches.cn: 入口是进入发生的地点。

branches.en: A recorded item is what has been entered in a book.
branches.cn: 记录条目是被写进书里的内容。

branches.en: A contest entry is what has been entered in a competition.
branches.cn: 参赛作品是被投进比赛的东西。

branches.en: The bare act of entering is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 纯粹的进入动作是最古老的含义。

branches.en: A doorway exists for the act of entering.
branches.cn: 入口正是为了进入的动作而存在。

intro.en: Entry grows from Latin intrare and Old French entree, with English relatives enter, entrance, and entrant.
intro.cn: entry 源自拉丁语 intrare 与古法语 entree，英语亲属词有 enter、entrance 与 entrant。

latinIntro.en: Latin intrare means to enter, built on intra, within.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 intrare 意为进入，建立在 intra（在内）之上。

items.example: Intra marks the inside of a place.
items.exampleCN: intra 标示一个地方的内部。

items.example: Intrare is the direct Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: intrare 是直接的拉丁语动词。

items.example: Entree carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: entree 把这个词带入法语。

items.meaning: a way in or a recorded item
items.exampleCN: entry 保留两种古老含义。

items.example: Enter is the short English verb.
items.exampleCN: enter 是简短的英语动词。

items.example: An entrant is someone who enters.
The ending of entry marks a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: entry 的词尾标示动作名词。

definition_zh: 缠绕；交织；使紧密相连
definition_en: to twist or wind things together so that they form one strand
core_image: 两股麻绳在指尖被拧成一股，再也分不出哪根是哪根
scene: 两家人因一场婚事结为一体，此后命运再也分不开。Two families became entwined through a single marriage.
sceneCN: 这里 entwine 是「交织；紧密相连」（第 2 个义项：抽象事物彼此缠绕）；句意：一场婚事把两个家族缠绕在一起。

senses.title: To twist strands into one
senses.definition: to wind two or more threads or wires around each other
senses.definitionCN: 把两根以上的线或丝互相绕紧
senses.example: The craftsperson entwines hemp and silk.
senses.exampleCN: 工匠把麻线与丝线捻在一起。
senses.why: The stem names twisting twice over, so the verb describes strands that lose their separate identity.
senses.whyCN: 词干本义是拧上两遍，因此动词描述失去各自动独立形态的线股。

senses.title: To link lives or ideas closely
senses.definition: to connect people, events, or themes so that they cannot be separated
senses.definitionCN: 把人、事件或主题连接得无法分开
senses.example: Trade entwined the two port cities.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易把两座港口城市连在一起。
senses.why: Applied to abstractions, the physical twisting becomes a relation of mutual dependence.
senses.whyCN: 用于抽象事物时，实体的拧转变成相互依存的关系。

senses.title: To encircle with something twined
senses.definition: to surround or decorate by winding something around a body or object
senses.definitionCN: 通过绕缠某物来包围或装饰身体或器物
senses.example: Climbers entwined the trunk with rope.
senses.exampleCN: 攀爬者用绳索绕住树干。
senses.why: Here the object of winding is external, so the verb means to wrap rather than to merge.
senses.whyCN: 此时被缠绕的是外物，因此动词指包绕而非合一。

intro.en: Entwine pairs the prefix en- with twine, a native word for a strand twisted twice.
intro.cn: entwine 由前缀 en- 加本族词 twine 构成，twine 指拧了两次的线股。

items.en: A root meaning two produced words for doubling.
items.cn: 表二义的词根产出众多双义派生词。

items.en: Twinum named a thread twisted double.
items.cn: twinum 指双股拧成的线。

items.en: Twine becomes both noun and verb in craft use.
items.cn: 中古英语 twine 在工艺语境兼作名词与动词。

items.en: Entwine is attested in poetry and rope work.
items.cn: 近代早期 entwine 见于诗歌与绳艺记录。

items.en: The word feels literary, common in descriptions of plants and fates.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词带文学色彩，常用于植物与命运描写。

note.en: Group one holds the twine family and rhyming builds; group two holds other verbs of joining.
note.cn: 第一组是 twine 同族与同尾词；第二组是其他表示连合的动词。

entries.definition: The noun and verb of twisting, which supplies the stem.
entries.definitionCN: 表拧转的名词与动词，提供词干。

entries.definition: Adds inter-, stressing that both sides twist into each other.
entries.definitionCN: 加 inter-，强调双方互绕。

entries.definition: Frequent as an adjective of hands, hair, and histories.
entries.definitionCN: 常作形容词，修饰手、发与历史。

entries.definition: Built on wind rather than twine, and rarer still.
entries.definitionCN: 以 wind 为词干，比 entwine 更生僻。

entries.definition: To twist into a snarl; the result is trouble rather than unity.
entries.definitionCN: 乱绕成结，结果是麻烦而非一体。

entries.definition: To pass strands alternately, common in metalwork and design.
entries.definitionCN: 线股交替穿过，常见于金工与设计。

entries.definition: To make fabric by crossing threads at right angles.
entries.definitionCN: 以垂直交织成织物。

entries.definition: To weave three or more strands into a patterned length.
entries.definitionCN: 把三股以上编成有花纹的一束。

normalIntro.en: En plus twine: to put things into the state of a doubled strand.
normalIntro.cn: en 加 twine：使事物变成双股合一线的状态。

normal.en: Two or more strands are needed; one cannot entwine alone.
normal.cn: 需要两股以上，单股无法 entwine。

normal.en: Literary style prefers entwine where everyday speech says mix.
normal.cn: 文学语体用 entwine，日常说 mix。

normal.en: Entwined fingers is a stock image of intimacy.
normal.cn: 十指交扣是表现亲密的固定意象。

normal.en: Use with passive for plants: the gate was entwined with roses.
normal.cn: 写植物时常用被动：大门被玫瑰缠绕。

normal.en: Do not swap with entangle, which implies a mess.
normal.cn: 不要与 entangle 互换，后者含混乱之意。

abstract.en: Picture two ropes becoming a single thicker rope.
abstract.cn: 想象两根绳拧成一根更粗的绳。

abstract.en: Imagine ivy climbing a doorframe in slow spirals.
abstract.cn: 想象常春藤沿门框缓缓盘旋而上。

abstract.en: Think of two family trees whose branches grow into each other.
abstract.cn: 想想两棵家谱树的枝杈相互长在一起。

examples.en: She entwined the two cables for extra strength.
examples.cn: 她把两股电缆绞在一起以增加强度。

examples.en: Their fortunes were entwined by one contract.
examples.cn: 一纸合同把他们的命运绑在一起。

examples.en: Ivy entwines the old wall each summer.
examples.cn: 每年夏天常春藤都会缠上那堵旧墙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因双拧」——因为两股一起拧，所以 entwine 是缠绕交织；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 原始日耳曼语表二义词根 → 古英语 twinum（双股线）→ 中古英语 twine＋en- → entwine，核心义「拧成一股」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts with rope work, moves to binding lives together, and ends with wrapping around an object.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词起于绳索工艺，转向把命运绑定，最后指环绕某物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: separate strands losing their edges as they are twisted together.
core.cn: 核心意象：各股线在拧转中失去彼此边界。

branches.en: Craft work supplies the literal base sense.
branches.cn: 工艺操作提供本义基础。

branches.en: Abstraction turns twisting into interdependence.
branches.cn: 抽象化把拧转变为相互依存。

branches.en: Wrapping keeps the strands distinct but enclosing.
branches.cn: 包绕让线股仍分明却形成围合。

branches.en: Both describe hands working with cord.
branches.cn: 两者都描述双手与绳线作业。

branches.en: Marriages and ivy both enclose what they touch.
branches.cn: 婚姻与藤蔓都会围住所接触之物。

intro.en: A native prefix and a native stem produce a family that stays mostly English.
intro.cn: 本族前缀配本族词干，词族基本保持英语本色。

latinIntro.en: Latin Du_o and plicare supplied learned rivals such as duplicate and plait.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 duo 与 plicare 提供了 duplicate 与 plait 之类的书面竞争词。

items.exampleCN: en- 位于 entwine 开头。

items.example: Twice keeps the same numeric idea.
items.exampleCN: twice 保留同一数字概念。

items.example: The form works as an adjective.

items.meaning: to form a ring of flowers

definition_zh: 逐一列举；枚举；计数
definition_en: to mention or list things one by one in order
core_image: 演讲者竖起手指，一条一条把要点数到最后一根
scene: 报告逐条列出整改事项。The report enumerates each corrective measure.
sceneCN: 这里 enumerate 是「逐一列举」（第 1 个义项：按顺序一条一条说出）；句意：报告逐条列出整改措施。

senses.title: To list items one by one
senses.definition: to name each member of a set in order instead of summarising it
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序说出集合中每一个成员，而非笼统概括
senses.example: The witness enumerated the vehicles she saw.
senses.exampleCN: 证人把她见到的车辆逐一列出。
senses.why: The Latin stem is about number, so the verb treats a list as something counted item by item.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干与数目相关，因此动词把清单看作逐项计数的对象。

senses.title: To count or reckon up formally
senses.definition: to go through things so as to establish how many there are
senses.definitionCN: 逐件清点以确定数量
senses.example: Clerks enumerated the ballots overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 职员通宵清点选票。
senses.why: Older administrative use kept the arithmetic sense that the listing sense grew from.
senses.whyCN: 较早的行政用法保留了产生列举义的那层算术含义。

senses.title: To step through items in a program
senses.definition: in computing, to access the members of a data collection in sequence
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域指按序访问数据集合的成员
senses.example: The loop enumerates every record in the table.
senses.exampleCN: 这段循环遍历表中的每条记录。
senses.why: Programming borrowed the word for the act of running through a list, keeping the one-by-one idea.
senses.whyCN: 编程借用该词表示跑完整个列表，保留逐条进行的含义。

intro.en: Enumerate joins a prefix of out to numerare, to number, from numerus, number.
intro.cn: enumerate 由表出的前缀加 numerare（计数）构成，numerus 意为数目。

items.en: Numerus means number, and numerare means to count.
items.cn: numerus 指数目，numerare 指计数。

items.en: Exnumerare shaped the compound with an out prefix.
items.cn: exnumerare 以表出的前缀塑成复合词。

items.en: Enumeratus names a thing counted through.
items.cn: enumeratus 指清点完毕之物。

items.en: English scholars take enumerate into formal prose.
items.cn: 十六世纪学者把 enumerate 带入正式书面语。

items.en: Statistics and law adopt enumeration as a technical noun.
items.cn: 十九世纪统计与法律采纳 enumeration 作技术名词。

items.en: Computing renews the verb for sequences of records.
items.cn: 现代英语中计算机领域让该动词在记录序列中复活。

note.en: Group one holds the numerus family; group two holds other verbs of listing.
note.cn: 第一组是 numerus 词族；第二组是其他列举动词。

entries.definition: The action noun used in statistics, law, and computing.
entries.definitionCN: 动作名词，用于统计、法律与计算机。

entries.definition: Same stem with a negating prefix, meaning too many to count.
entries.definitionCN: 同词干加否定前缀，指多到数不清。

entries.definition: To put into numbers; the sense enumerate generalises.
entries.definitionCN: 使成数字，enumerate 将其义项泛化。

entries.definition: Sounds similar but means to flow out from a source.
entries.definitionCN: 读音相近但义为从源头流出。

entries.definition: The everyday way of writing items down in order.
entries.definitionCN: 按序写下条目的日常说法。

entries.definition: To set out each item separately, close in register.
entries.definitionCN: 逐条分列，语体接近。

entries.definition: To describe the parts fully, with less emphasis on order.
entries.definitionCN: 详尽描述各部分，较少强调顺序。

entries.definition: To record items in a fixed classification system.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定分类体系登记条目。

normalIntro.en: Inside enumerate sits numerate, so the verb is counting done out loud.
normalIntro.cn: enumerate 内含 numerate，因此这个动词是出声的计数。

normal.en: Use it when order matters: first, second, third.
normal.cn: 强调顺序时使用：第一、第二、第三。

normal.en: Enumerate is formal; list is neutral.
normal.cn: enumerate 正式，list 中性。

normal.en: The noun enumeration appears in reports and code names.
normal.cn: 名词 enumeration 常见于报告与代码命名。

normal.en: Avoid it for mere description; it demands countable items.
normal.cn: 不要用于单纯描述，它要求可数的条目。

normal.en: In code, enumerate a list to get index and value pairs.
normal.cn: 在代码中 enumerate 列表可同时得到序号与值。

abstract.en: Picture fingers rising one at a time as each item is named.
abstract.cn: 想象每说一条就竖起一根手指。

abstract.en: Imagine a clipboard checked line by line.
abstract.cn: 想象逐行核对的写字板清单。

abstract.en: Think of a clerk moving along a column of figures.
abstract.cn: 想想沿数字列逐行移动的办事员。

examples.en: She enumerated the risks without pausing.
examples.cn: 她毫不停顿地逐条列出风险。

examples.en: The manual enumerates the safety steps.
examples.cn: 手册逐条列出安全步骤。

examples.en: Please enumerate the items you need quoted.
examples.cn: 请逐一列出需要报价的项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一纽美瑞特」——音近 enumerate，像把每纽美玉都数一遍，所以是逐一列举；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。」

root: 拉丁语 numerus（数目）→ numerare（计数）→ 过去分词 enumeratus → 英语 enumerate，核心义「一项一项数出来」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb runs from counting objects, to naming items in order, to stepping through data in code.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从清点实物，到按序命名条目，再到代码中遍历数据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one finger raised for each item until the list is spent.
core.cn: 核心意象：每说一条竖起一根手指，直到数完。

branches.en: Listing in words is the common prose sense.
branches.cn: 用语言逐条列出是最通行的散文义。

branches.en: Counting keeps the arithmetic root alive.
branches.cn: 清点实物让算术词根保持活力。

branches.en: Code formalises the sequence as an operation.
branches.cn: 代码把序列固化为一项操作。

branches.en: Both require discrete countable items.
branches.cn: 两者都要求分立可数的对象。

branches.en: Prose and program both walk a list end to end.
branches.cn: 书面语与程序都从头到尾走完列表。

intro.en: A Latin numeral stem takes verbal and nominal endings through two learned layers.
intro.cn: 拉丁数词词干经两层书面借用取得动词与名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin Numerus means number, numerare to count, and enumeratus counted out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 numerus 指数目，numerare 指数数，enumeratus 指已数出。

items.exampleCN: e- 标记数出这一动作。

items.example: A modern coinage on the stem.
items.exampleCN: 基于该词干的现代新词。

definition_zh: 清晰发音；明确阐述
definition_en: to pronounce words clearly, or to state an idea in a firm and definite way
core_image: 播音员把每个音节咬得边界分明，话筒前的声音像被刀切过
scene: 台词老师要求学生把每个音节说清楚。The coach asked every actor to enunciate each syllable.
sceneCN: 这里 enunciate 是「清晰发音」（第 1 个义项：把字音说得分明）；句意：教练要求每位演员把每个音节念清楚。

senses.title: To pronounce words distinctly
senses.definition: to shape the sounds of speech so that each word is heard clearly
senses.definitionCN: 把语音成形，使每个词都听得清楚
senses.example: She enunciates so well that subtitles are unnecessary.
senses.exampleCN: 她吐字极清楚，根本不需要字幕。
senses.why: The Latin stem is about reporting, and clear speech is a report that reaches the listener intact.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干本义与宣告有关，清楚的吐字就是一份完好送达的报告。

senses.title: To state a doctrine or policy firmly
senses.definition: to express a principle, aim, or rule in definite terms
senses.definitionCN: 用确定的措辞表达原则、目标或规则
senses.example: The charter enunciates three core values.
senses.exampleCN: 章程阐明了三项核心价值。
senses.why: Formal writing transfers the speech sense to statements that must be beyond doubt.
senses.whyCN: 正式书面语把吐定义项转移到不容含糊的声明上。

intro.en: Enunciate joins a prefix of out to Latin nuntiare, to report, from nuntius, a messenger.
intro.cn: enunciate 由表出的前缀加拉丁语 nuntiare（报告）构成，nuntius 指信使。

items.en: Nuntius means messenger or report.
items.cn: nuntius 指信使或报告。

items.en: Nuntiare means to bring word, and enuntiare to state out.
items.cn: nuntiare 指传信，enuntiare 指明白说出。

items.en: Enuntiatus marks a thing definitely declared.
items.cn: enuntiatus 标记已被明确宣告之事。

items.en: English adopts the verb in rhetorical and elocution texts.
items.cn: 十八世纪英语在修辞与朗读教材中采纳该词。

items.en: Speech therapy keeps the pronunciation sense alive.
items.cn: 现代英语中语音治疗保留发音义。

note.en: Group one holds the nuntiare family; group two holds other verbs of saying clearly.
note.cn: 第一组是 nuntiare 词族；第二组是其他表示说清的动词。

entries.definition: The action noun used in voice training and in formal statements.
entries.definitionCN: 动作名词，用于发声训练与正式声明。

entries.definition: Built on the same report root with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 同一报告词根搭配别的前缀。

entries.definition: To declare or to shape sounds, the closest rival in speech use.
entries.definitionCN: 宣告或发出字音，是发音义上最近的竞争词。

entries.definition: To accuse publicly, keeping the reporting idea in a hostile direction.
entries.definitionCN: 公开指控，报告义转向敌意方向。

entries.definition: To express coherently, with the image of jointed sounds.
entries.definitionCN: 有条理地表达，取关节分明之音的意象。

entries.definition: The neutral verb for putting something in words.
entries.definitionCN: 用语言表达的中性动词。

entries.definition: To announce formally, closer to the doctrinal sense.
entries.definitionCN: 正式宣告，接近教义阐意义。

entries.definition: A fixed collocation in acting and speech coaching.
entries.definitionCN: 表演与朗读教学中的固定搭配。

normalIntro.en: Enunciate shares its core with nuntiare, to bring word, so think of a message delivered crisply.
normalIntro.cn: enunciate 与 nuntiare（传信）共享核心，可想成一条送达利落的消息。

normal.en: For speech, use it without an object: practice enunciating.
normal.cn: 表发音时可不带宾语：practice enunciating。

normal.en: For ideas, it takes a doctrine, policy, or principle.
normal.cn: 表思想时宾语多为学说、政策或原则。

normal.en: The noun enunciation appears in drama schools.
normal.cn: 名词 enunciation 常出现在戏剧院校。

normal.en: Pronounce is everyday; enunciate stresses clarity.
normal.cn: pronounce 日常，enunciate 强调清晰度。

normal.en: Do not write envelope here; the ending is -ciate.
normal.cn: 不要写成 envelope；词尾是 -ciate。

abstract.en: Picture a metronome ticking each syllable in place.
abstract.cn: 想象节拍器把每个音节敲到位。

abstract.en: Imagine a town crier reading a proclamation aloud.
abstract.cn: 想象报信人当众宣读告示。

abstract.en: Think of glass beads laid out one by one on a tray.
abstract.cn: 想想木盘上一颗颗摆开的玻璃珠。

examples.en: The announcer enunciates every number on the board.
examples.cn: 播音员把板上每个数字都念得清楚。

examples.en: The manifesto enunciates a right to housing.
examples.cn: 宣言明确阐述居住权。

examples.en: Slowing down helps you enunciate better.
examples.cn: 放慢语速有助于吐字更清晰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一南谁累特」——音近 enunciate，报信的人一路喊到累，所以是清晰宣告；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 nuntius（信使）→ nuntiare（报告）→ enuntiare（明白宣告）→ 英语 enunciate，核心义「把话说清、把义宣明」。

sensesIntro.en: One sense lives in the mouth and the other in official writing, both demanding distinctness.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个义项在口中，一个在公文里，两者都要求分明。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a message spoken so cleanly that nothing is smudged.
core.cn: 核心意象：话说得极干净，绝无模糊之处。

branches.en: Physical articulation is the concrete sense.
branches.cn: 口部发音是具体义项。

branches.en: Formal statements borrow the same distinctness.
branches.cn: 正式声明借用同一分明特质。

branches.en: Both require that the receiver hear without effort.
branches.cn: 两者都要求听者毫不费力地接收。

branches.en: Voice training keeps only the muscular sense.
branches.cn: 发声训练只保留肌肉层面的义项。

branches.en: Legal and political prose keep the declaring sense.
branches.cn: 法律与政治文体保留宣告义项。

intro.en: A Latin prefix of out plus a stem of reporting takes English verbal endings.
intro.cn: 拉丁语表出的前缀加报告词干，再取英语动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin Nuntius is messenger, nuntiare is to report, and nuncupare is to name aloud.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nuntius 指信使，nuntiare 指报告，nuncupare 指高声命名。

items.exampleCN: e- 标记说出这一动作。

definition_zh: 包围；笼罩；覆盖
definition_en: to cover, surround, or close in around something completely
core_image: 浓雾从四面包上来，山谷、道路与屋顶一起消失在白幕里
scene: 清晨的大雾把整片河谷裹住。Dense fog enveloped the whole valley.
sceneCN: 这里 envelop 是「笼罩；包围」（第 1 个义项：从四周完全盖住）；句意：浓雾笼罩了整个河谷。

senses.title: To cover something on every side
senses.definition: to surround a thing so that it cannot be seen or reached
senses.definitionCN: 从四周围住某物，使其无法看见或触及
senses.example: Flames enveloped the upper floor.
senses.exampleCN: 火焰吞没了上层楼面。
senses.why: The Latin stem means to roll in, and rolling something all the way around is exactly covering.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干意为卷入，把四周滚满正是彻底覆盖。

senses.title: To close in around a military force
senses.definition: to surround troops or a position so that escape is cut off
senses.definitionCN: 包围军队或阵地，切断其退路
senses.example: Two brigades enveloped the crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 两个旅包围了渡口。
senses.why: Doctrine borrowed the word for the manoeuvre that wraps around an enemy flank.
senses.whyCN: 军事条令借用这个词指包抄敌军侧翼的机动。

senses.title: To take something up so it loses its outline
senses.definition: to absorb a smaller thing into a larger atmosphere or situation
senses.definitionCN: 把较小的事物吸收进更大的氛围或情境之中
senses.example: The crowd enveloped the returning runner.
senses.exampleCN: 人群把归来的跑者团团围住。
senses.why: Extended to feelings and crowds, the verb describes losing edges rather than physical covering.
senses.whyCN: 延伸到情绪与人群时，动词描述的是边界的消失而非实体覆盖。

intro.en: Envelop comes from Old French envellir, built on Latin involvere, to roll into.
intro.cn: envelop 来自古法语 envellir，建立在拉丁语 involvere（卷入）之上。

items.en: Volvere means to roll or turn.
items.cn: volvere 意为滚动或转动。

items.en: Involvere means to roll in or wrap up.
items.cn: involvere 意为卷入或包裹。

items.en: Envellir and envoler carry the rolling sense into French.
items.cn: envellir 与 envoler 把滚动义带入法语。

items.en: English records envelop as a verb of wrapping.
items.cn: 中古英语记录 envelop，表包裹。

items.en: Military writing fixes the sense of encircling a foe.
items.cn: 十九世纪军事文体固定包围敌军之义。

items.en: The noun envelope keeps the paper wrapper sense.
items.cn: 现代英语中名词 envelope 保留纸封套义。

note.en: Group one holds the volvere family and the paper noun; group two holds other verbs of surrounding.
note.cn: 第一组是 volvere 词族与纸封名词；第二组是其他表包围的动词。

entries.definition: The paper wrapper or a covering layer, spelled with an extra letter.
entries.definitionCN: 纸封套或覆盖层，拼写多一个字母。

entries.definition: The state or manoeuvre of surrounding, common in tactics.
entries.definitionCN: 包围状态或机动，战术用语常见。

entries.definition: To roll into a situation, hence to include or implicate.
entries.definitionCN: 卷入情境，引申为包含或牵连。

entries.definition: To roll back around, used of orbits and repeated questions.
entries.definitionCN: 绕回转动，用于轨道与反复讨论。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for being all around something.
entries.definitionCN: 表四周环绕的日常动词。
